primary_topics: Forum address at the ACCRA Law 40th Anniversary, November 29, 2012 -- invited by Chairman Ave Cruz; addressed to the Management Association of the Philippines (MAP)

CJP's answer to 'How can the judiciary help the economy?': by deferring as much as possible to the political branches of government on economic controversies; strict scrutiny for civil liberties; deferential interpretation for economic matters

Three landmark SC decisions analyzed: Tanada v. Angara (WTO upheld; court must not second-guess elected branches' economic decisions); La Bugal-B'Laan v. Ramos (Mining Law upheld 10-4 on MFR; Constitution should not strangulate economic growth); Gamboa v. Teves (60-40 limited to voting shares; CJP urges prospective application)
The Philippines' 2012 economic performance: best in ASEAN (6.5% for first nine months); second in Asia after China; judicial deference to political branches enabled this growth
sub_topics: Ave Cruz occasion: ACCRA Law 40th Anniversary; CJP's tribute to Ave -- had Ave accepted Cory Aquino's SC offer in 1986, 'there would have been no Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr. and Chief Justice Artemio V. Panganiban'

Liberty and Prosperity philosophy: to close his CJ term, convened Global Forum on Liberty and Prosperity (October 18-20, 2006); 300+ jurists and lawyers; CJ Beverley McLachlin of Canada suggested adding 'Under the Rule of Law'; stayed three more days after the Forum; 'fell in love with the Philippines'

Philippines 2012 GDP: 6.3% Q1, 5.9% Q2, 7.1% Q3; 6.5% overall for first nine months; best in ASEAN; second in Asia after China -- demonstrates that judicial deference to political branches enabled economic growth

Judiciary's role: 'in judging controversies involving the economy, the judiciary must defer as much as possible to the political branches of government, the President and Congress in collaboration with the private sector'
Two-fold standard: strict scrutiny for political and civil liberties (scales weigh against government); deferential interpretation for economic matters (absent grave abuse of discretion)

Tanada v. Angara (May 2, 1997): WTO Treaty upheld; court refused to pass upon the wisdom of globalization; 'What the Senate did in ratifying the WTO Treaty was a valid exercise of its authority. As to whether such exercise was wise... is outside the realm of judicial inquiry'

La Bugal-B'Laan v. Ramos: original 8-5 struck down Mining Law; on MFR, court reversed 10-4 (CJP as ponente); 'The Constitution should be read in broad, life-giving strokes. It should not be used to strangulate economic growth or to serve narrow, parochial interests'

Gamboa v. Teves (June 28, 2011): SC limited 60-40 rule to voting shares in public utilities; dissenters argued it should cover entire capital stock (as interpreted since 1935 by DOJ and SEC); CJP's position: 'I submit that the judiciary does not have the mandate, not to say the expertise, to decide on matters relating to the economy'; urges prospective application to protect good-faith investors

stances.claim: The judiciary can best help the economy by deferring to the political branches on economic matters -- 'the judiciary does not have the mandate, not to say the expertise, to decide on matters relating to the economy.' The Philippines' best-in-ASEAN GDP growth in 2012 is the empirical evidence that judicial deference works.
stances.rhetorical_move: GDP-as-empirical-proof: the Philippines' 7.1% Q3 growth as the quantitative evidence that judicial deference to elected economic decision-makers produces results
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing principle with contemporary empirical support

stances.claim: The La Bugal Mining Law reversal encapsulates the correct constitutional philosophy: 'The Constitution should be read in broad, life-giving strokes. It should not be used to strangulate economic growth or to serve narrow, parochial interests. Rather, it should be construed to grant Congress and the President sufficient discretion and reasonable leeway to attract foreign investments and expertise, and to secure the blessings of prosperity and peace.'
stances.rhetorical_move: life-giving-strokes argument: the Constitution as a living document that enables economic growth, not a rigid text that protects narrow interests
stances.confidence: asserted as the definitive constitutional philosophy in the La Bugal ponencia

stances.claim: Gamboa v. Teves should be applied prospectively: 'many foreign investors have brought their capital here' relying on the DOJ/SEC interpretation that the 60% applies to entire capital stock. Penalizing these good-faith investors retroactively would be unfair and would damage foreign investment confidence in the Philippines.
stances.rhetorical_move: good-faith-reliance argument: retroactive application of a new constitutional interpretation as a violation of the fairness principle that underlies investor confidence

notable_anecdotes: Ave Cruz and the three non-existent CJs: 'After the EDSA people power revolution in 1986, President Corazon Aquino offered Ave a seat in the Supreme Court. However, he respectfully declined... Had he accepted President Cory Aquino's offer, he could have been Chief Justice a decade later. And there would have been no Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr. and Chief Justice Artemio V. Panganiban.'

CJ McLachlin fell in love with the Philippines: after the Global Forum she stayed three more days; 'she fell in love with the Philippines' -- prompting her suggestion to add 'Under the Rule of Law' to CJP's philosophy.

Philippines best in ASEAN in 2012: 6.3% Q1, 5.9% Q2, 7.1% Q3; 6.5% overall -- 'best performer in the ASEAN Region and the second best in Asia, second only to China.' This is the empirical evidence CJP cites for why judicial deference works.

La Bugal Constitution read in broad strokes: 'The Constitution should be read in broad, life-giving strokes. It should not be used to strangulate economic growth or to serve narrow, parochial interests. Rather, it should be construed to grant Congress and the President sufficient discretion and reasonable leeway to enable them to attract foreign investments and expertise.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 29, 2012 at the ACCRA Law 40th Anniversary forum -- addressed to the Management Association of the Philippines, invited by Chairman Avelino V. Cruz -- this address by CJP opens with the Ave Cruz counterfactual ('he could have been Chief Justice a decade later... there would have been no Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr. and Chief Justice Artemio V. Panganiban') and congratulates BPI President Aurelio Montinola III on being named MAP Management Man of the Year 2012 ('well deserved and, in fact, long overdue'). He describes the October 2006 Global Forum on Liberty and Prosperity (300+ jurists; Canadian CJ Beverley McLachlin suggested 'Under the Rule of Law' and 'fell in love with the Philippines, staying three more days after the Forum'). The speech's central answer: 'the judiciary must defer as much as possible to the political branches of government' on economic controversies -- empirically validated by the Philippines' best-in-ASEAN 2012 GDP growth (6.3% Q1, 5.9% Q2, 7.1% Q3; 6.5% for nine months; second in Asia after China). He presents three landmark decisions: Tanada v. Angara (May 1997 -- WTO upheld; 'what the Senate did was a valid exercise of its authority; whether it was wise is outside judicial inquiry'); La Bugal-B'Laan v. Ramos (original 8-5 struck down the Mining Law; MFR reversed it 10-4 with CJP as ponente -- 'The Constitution should be read in broad, life-giving strokes. It should not be used to strangulate economic growth'); and Gamboa v. Teves (June 2011 -- 60-40 rule limited to voting shares; CJP urges prospective application since foreign investors relied in good faith on the prior DOJ/SEC interpretation that the limit covers entire capital stock). He closes: 'In matters affecting the prosperity of our people, the judiciary can help the economy by deferring to the political branches of the government and to the private business sector which is the recognized engine of growth in a regime of free enterprise.'
